title: The Wrong Bus
author: Tadoku Note (original)
summary: スコットランド旅行中のユウタは、乗るバスを間違えて知らない村へ。思いがけない一日が始まります。

source.note: Original text written for this app.

paragraphs: Yuta was twenty-two, and this was his first trip abroad alone. He was in Edinburgh, in Scotland, and today he wanted to see a famous old castle by the sea. He checked the bus number on his phone: the 43. He waited at the bus stop in the rain.

A green bus came. Yuta was looking at his phone, and he only saw the number 4 on the front. He got on, paid the driver and sat at the back. He was very tired, and the bus was warm. Soon he fell asleep.
When he woke up, there was no sea. There were hills, and a lot of sheep. The bus was empty. Only Yuta and the driver were on it.
Yuta walked to the front. “Excuse me,” he said. “Is this the bus to the castle?”
The driver laughed. “The castle? No, son. This is the 4A. This bus goes to Glenmuir. It’s the last stop.”
“Glenmuir?” Yuta looked at the map on his phone. Glenmuir was a tiny village, sixty kilometers from the castle. “When is the next bus back?”
“Tomorrow morning,” said the driver. “Seven o’clock.”
The bus stopped. Yuta got off. The village had one street, one church, one shop and one pub. The rain stopped, and the sun came out. The hills were very green. “Well,” thought Yuta, “I am here now.”
He went into the pub. It was small and warm, and there was a fire. Five or six people were sitting at the tables. They all turned and looked at him.
“Hello,” said Yuta. “I took the wrong bus.”
Everybody laughed, but it was a friendly laugh. A woman behind the bar said, “Then you are very welcome to Glenmuir! I’m Fiona. Sit down by the fire. Are you hungry?”

Fiona gave him a bowl of hot soup and some bread. An old man with a white beard sat down next to him. His name was Angus. He was a farmer, and he had two hundred sheep. “Where are you from?” he asked.
“Japan,” said Yuta. “From Osaka.”
“Japan!” said Angus. “My grandson lives in Japan. He teaches English in a place called... Nara?”
“Nara is very near Osaka!” said Yuta. He showed Angus photos of the deer in Nara on his phone. Angus laughed and laughed. “Deer that bow to people! I must visit him.”

In the afternoon, Angus took Yuta to his farm. Yuta helped him move the sheep from one field to another. It was not easy. The sheep did not want to go. Angus’s dog, Bess, did most of the work. Yuta mostly ran around and fell in the mud. Angus laughed again.

That evening, there was music in the pub. Two men played the violin, and a young woman sang old Scottish songs. Then they asked Yuta to sing a song from Japan. He was shy, but he sang a song his grandmother taught him. Everybody clapped.
Fiona had a small room above the pub, and Yuta slept there. It was very quiet. He could hear only the wind and, sometimes, a sheep.

At seven the next morning, the bus came. Fiona gave him a sandwich for the trip. Angus came too. He gave Yuta a piece of paper with his grandson’s address in Nara. “Visit him,” he said. “Tell him his grandfather taught you how to move sheep.”
Yuta got on the bus. This time, he checked the number very carefully.

Later that day, he finally saw the famous castle. It was beautiful. But when he went home to Japan, his friends asked, “What was the best part of your trip?” And Yuta always said the same thing: “The wrong bus.”
